results.title: lsio_trigger_o 在复位后被无条件拉高，脱离 TX/RX watermark 触发条件。
results.analysis_reason: This bug was not one of the original findings, but the RTL directly confirms it. The surrounding comment says `lsio_trigger_o` is a registered LSIO DMA handshake trigger asserted when data thresholds are considered met. However, after reset the sequential block unconditionally assigns `lsio_trigger_o <= 1'b1` every cycle, with no dependency on `event_tx_watermark`, `event_rx_watermark`, FIFO depth, RX empty status, or any other threshold predicate. This makes the LSIO/DMA trigger permanently asserted once reset is released.
results.trigger_condition: After `rst_ni` is deasserted, regardless of UART FIFO level, watermark configuration, RX/TX activity, or interrupt status.
results.security_impact: Downstream LSIO/DMA logic can observe a persistent UART trigger unrelated to the actual UART watermark predicates, potentially causing spurious DMA service or stale/empty UART data handling depending on integration.

results.title: UART break interrupt 重新 armed 条件过弱，未要求 RX 线保持高电平至少半个 bit-time。
results.analysis_reason: This bug was not one of the original findings. The UART documentation states that only one interrupt is generated per break and that the line must return high for at least half a bit-time before another break interrupt is generated. The RTL break FSM enters `BRK_WAIT` after `event_rx_break_err`, but exits back to `BRK_CHK` whenever `rx_in` is sampled high once. There is no half-bit-time counter, baud tick qualification, or stability window in `BRK_WAIT`. A short high pulse can therefore re-arm break detection earlier than the documented contract.
results.trigger_condition: A line break is detected, the FSM enters `BRK_WAIT`, and `rx_in` briefly samples high for less than half a bit-time before returning low.
results.security_impact: The UART can generate repeated break interrupts from a single long break with a short high glitch, violating the documented rate/arming contract and enabling interrupt amplification or misleading line-break status behavior.
